What specific techniques can someone use to be viewed as a good conversationalist?
I'll add looking people in the eyes.

Listen. Everyone really just want to talk. So if you actually listen and pay attention then comment on what they said. They will swear you were the one who was doing all the talking and doing it well.

Aside from the obvious things like ask questions, listen, eye contact, I actually think disagreeing is an important part of being good conversationalist too. Maybe it's cultural, but I think Americans are too quick to agree all the time (nod, smile, "I know right!?") to build rapport. It is important in building trust, but also being able to thoughtfully disagree without being a dick shows that you're listening, understanding, and thinking critically about what the other person is saying. It makes for a more meaningful conversation and in my experience has made people more memorable.

be genuinely interested in learning other peoples interests.

My uncle told me this when I was about 16. I am always surrounded by teachers.

"People raise their voice/yell because they don't feel that they are being heard."

This has really stuck with me when I'm in conflict with another person and they start shouting or getting more aggressive in their approach. I've gotten to the point that when I see that happening, it prompts me to take a step back and acknowledge what they are saying, validate, empathize, etc. I find that most of the time, once the person feels heard (even if you don't agree) they start to calm down, and a more rational, productive conversation can happen.

I've deescalated and resolved some pretty ugly arguments by employing this. And, who knows, maybe it's helped prevent me from getting murdered in a fit of rage. :)
